warnings: This source is Massachusetts M.G.L. c. 151B § 4, a fair housing and employment discrimination statute. It contains no rules about rent increases, just cause eviction, security deposits, application/screening fees, rental housing screening restrictions, or algorithmic rent-setting. The text addresses employment discrimination, housing discrimination based on protected characteristics (race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, genetic information, handicap, marital status, age, children, public assistance recipiency), wheelchair accessibility modifications, fair lending practices, and sexual harassment—but not the six rental-housing law categories in scope for this tool.

Section 10 prohibits discrimination against recipients of housing subsidies and public assistance, which is a screening restriction, but only as an employment/credit discrimination statute, not a rental housing regulation. The rental housing content (sections 4, 7B, 10–11, 13, 18) appears to define unfair housing practices, yet none establish affirmative rent, eviction, deposit, or algorithmic-pricing rules that tenants can verify at a specific address.
